acts.desc: Host Ira Glass reads famous last words from Bing Crosby, Oscar Wilde, W.C. Fields, and talks about what we want from people's last words.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Sarah Vowell tells the story of Page Smith and Eloise Pickard Smith. They were married for over five decades, and died a day apart. It's a story of people attempting to surround death in a web of words, of very eloquent people and their last words, and of what last words can and cannot accomplish.
acts.title: Actions Speak Louder

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Forty-five people read Luc Sante's story The Unknown Soldier, in which we hear about people's final moments, final thoughts.

songs.a: Leonard Cohen, performed by House of Love

acts.title: The Unknown Soldier

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Writer Greil Marcus explains what rock fans use dead rock stars for.

songs.a: The Sex Pistols, performed on the accordion

acts.title: How The Living Use The Dead

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: An act about which the less said, the better. (12 seconds)
acts.title: Rosebud

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: We go through transcripts from those black box flight recorders recovered from airplane crashes to see what people say. One pilot declares "I love you" to someone, another is doing his job like always and suddenly says, "uh-oh." It's an interview with Malcolm McPherson, author of The Black Box: All-New Cockpit Voice Recorder Accounts of In-Flight Accidents.
acts.title: Black Box

acts.label: Act Six
acts.desc: Writer Tobias Wolff reads his story "Bullet in the Brain" from his collection of stories The Night in Question, about a bank robbery and a man who's shot, and what he thinks about before he dies.
acts.title: What Goes Through Your Head
